# 4. Strings, characters and vectors

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

Strings are mutable sequences of Unicode characters; vectors are fixed-size,
indexed sequences of anything.

## Strings and characters

Indexes start at 0. Strings written in the source are constants; make-string,
string-copy and string build ones you can change.

`examples/strings.lisp`:

```scheme
(define greeting "Hello, cog-lisp")
(display (string-length greeting))
(newline)
(display (list (string-ref greeting 0) (substring greeting 7 15)))
(newline)
(write (string-append "cog" "-" "lisp"))
(newline)

; Searching and splitting.
(display (list (string-index greeting #\,) (string-search greeting "lisp")))
(newline)
(write (string-split "red,green,,blue" #\,))
(newline)
(write (string-join '("a" "b" "c") ", "))
(newline)

; Comparing (by character code) and case.
(display (list (string<? "apple" "banana") (string=? "x" "x" "x") (string-ci=? "LISP" "lisp")))
(newline)
(display (list (string-upcase "shout") (string-downcase "QUIET")))
(newline)

; Characters and their codes.
(display (list (char->integer #\A) (integer->char 955) (char-upcase #\q)))
(newline)
(display (map (lambda (c) (list c (char-alphabetic? c) (char-numeric? c)))
              (string->list "a1 ")))
(newline)

; Numbers to and from text.
(display (list (string->number "42") (string->number "2.5e3") (string->number "ff" 16)
               (string->number "forty-two") (number->string 255 2)))
(newline)

; Changing a string: copy the constant first.
(define name (string-copy "cat"))
(string-set! name 0 #\b)
(display name)
(newline)
(display (guard (e ((error-object? e) (error-object-message e)))
  (string-set! "cat" 0 #\b)))
(newline)

; A Caesar cipher, one character at a time.
(define (shift-char c k)
  (if (char-alphabetic? c)
      (let ((base (if (char-upper-case? c) 65 97)))
        (integer->char (+ base (modulo (+ (- (char->integer c) base) k) 26))))
      c))
(define (caesar s k) (list->string (map (lambda (c) (shift-char c k)) (string->list s))))
(define secret (caesar "Attack at dawn!" 3))
(display secret)
(newline)
(display (caesar secret -3))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
15
(H cog-lisp)
"cog-lisp"
(5 11)
("red" "green" "" "blue")
"a, b, c"
(#t #t #t)
(SHOUT quiet)
(65 λ Q)
((a #t #f) (1 #f #t) (  #f #f))
(42 2500.0 255 #f 11111111)
bat
string-set!: string is immutable (a literal); copy it first
Dwwdfn dw gdzq!
Attack at dawn!
```

## Writing any character in a string

`examples/escapes.lisp`:

```scheme
(define greek "\x3bb; is lambda, \x3c0; is pi")
(display greek)
(newline)
(display (string-length "\x3bb;"))
(newline)

; Escapes for the usual control characters.
(write (map char->integer (string->list "\t\n\r\a\b")))
(newline)

; write shows control characters so they cannot hide; display prints them as they are.
(define bell (string #\a (integer->char 7) #\b))
(write bell)
(newline)
(write (string (integer->char 1) (integer->char 27)))
(newline)

; Whatever write prints reads back as the same string.
(define tricky (string #\" #\\ (integer->char 0) (integer->char 31) #\x))
(display (equal? tricky (read (open-input-string (with-output-to-string (lambda () (write tricky)))))))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
λ is lambda, π is pi
1
(9 10 13 7 8)
"a\x7;b"
"\x1;\x1b;"
#t
```

## Format: text with ~ directives, as in Common Lisp

(format #f control arg ...) answers a string, (format #t ...) writes to the
current output, and (format port ...) to a port; (format control arg ...),
with the control string first, answers a string as SRFI 28 does. Each ~
directive takes what it needs from the arguments: ~A displays, ~S writes,
~D ~X ~B ~O print integers, ~F floats, ~% is a newline. Parameters and flags
go between the ~ and the letter: ~5D pads to five columns, ~:D groups digits
with commas, ~,2F rounds to two decimals. ~{ ~} loops over a list, ~^ leaves
it before the separator after the last element, ~[ ~; ~] chooses, ~:P and
~:@P make plurals, and ~( ~) changes case.

`examples/format.lisp`:

```scheme
(define (show s) (display s) (newline))

(show (format #f "~A has ~D item~:P, worth ~,2F." "Ada" 3 7.5))
(show (format #f "~5D|~5,'0D|~:D" 42 42 1234567))
(show (format #f "#x~X is ~D" 255 255))
(show (format #f "~{~A~^, ~}" '(red green blue)))
(show (format #f "~:{~A=~A ~}" '((a 1) (b 2))))
(show (format #f "~D pon~:@P and ~D pon~:@P" 1 3))
(show (format #f "~[none~;one~;two~:;many~] of them" 7))
(show (format #f "~:[off~;on~]" #t))
(show (format #f "~:(the quick brown fox~)"))
(show (format "SRFI 28 style: ~a, ~s" "plain" "written"))
(format #t "straight to the output~%")
```

Its output:

```text
Ada has 3 items, worth 7.50.
   42|00042|1,234,567
#xFF is 255
red, green, blue
a=1 b=2 
1 pony and 3 ponies
many of them
on
The Quick Brown Fox
SRFI 28 style: plain, "written"
straight to the output
```

## Fixed-size, indexed data

#(...) is a vector constant; make-vector, vector and vector-copy make ones you
can change. A vector is a Smalltalk Array, so it passes to Smalltalk as it is.

`examples/vectors.lisp`:

```scheme
(define primes #(2 3 5 7 11))
(display (list (vector-length primes) (vector-ref primes 2)))
(newline)
(write (vector->list primes 1 3))
(newline)
(write (vector-map (lambda (p) (* p p)) primes))
(newline)

; Building one up.
(define squares (make-vector 5 0))
(do ((i 0 (+ i 1))) ((= i 5))
  (vector-set! squares i (* i i)))
(write squares)
(newline)
(write (list (vector 'a "b" #\c) (vector-append #(1) #(2 3)) (subvector primes 3 5)))
(newline)

; Quasiquote works inside vectors.
(define n 42)
(write `#(answer ,n ,@(list 'and 'more)))
(newline)
(display (equal? #(1 (2 "x")) (vector 1 (list 2 "x"))))
(newline)

; An insertion sort, in place.
(define (vector-sort! v less?)
  (do ((i 1 (+ i 1))) ((>= i (vector-length v)) v)
    (let ((x (vector-ref v i)))
      (let loop ((j (- i 1)))
        (if (and (>= j 0) (less? x (vector-ref v j)))
            (begin (vector-set! v (+ j 1) (vector-ref v j))
                   (loop (- j 1)))
            (vector-set! v (+ j 1) x))))))
(write (vector-sort! (vector-copy #(31 4 15 9 26 5)) <))
(newline)
(write (vector-sort! (vector "pear" "fig" "apple") string<?))
(newline)

; Smalltalk sees an Array.
(display [#(3 1 2) asSortedCollection])
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(5 5)
(3 5)
#(4 9 25 49 121)
#(0 1 4 9 16)
(#(a "b" #\c) #(1 2 3) #(7 11))
#(answer 42 and more)
#t
#(4 5 9 15 26 31)
#("apple" "fig" "pear")
#<a SortedCollection(1 2 3)>
```
